sentence: This project studies whether targeting the activity of two specific factors can improve the response of childhood neuroblastoma to immunotherapy.
This project builds a workflow that measures in three dimensions how much therapeutic antibody reaches the brain, for Alzheimer's disease drug discovery.
This project studies genetic changes in children with inborn errors of immunity to find out how they affect immune cells and immune health.
This project builds statistical and machine learning methods that find the variants, genes and cell types behind severe mental illnesses such as schizophrenia.
This project develops instrumentation that combines image-guided histotripsy with thrombolytic drugs to treat chronic deep vein thrombosis.
This project tries to find out how to help transplanted stem cells engraft successfully in the bone marrow.
This project studies how cells control the level of a methyl donor called S-Adenosyl-methionine and how this links nutrients to chromatin methylation.
This project uses auricular vagus nerve stimulation to study inflammatory responses, nervous system functions and brain pathways in older adults with HIV-associated peripheral neuropathy.
This project studies how neutrophil serine proteases reshape the muscle stem cell niche after injury and affect muscle regeneration.
This project builds machine learning models and tests biomarkers to find people at high risk of pancreatic cancer and predict its metastases.
This project studies how certain mutations in non-small cell lung cancer affect the tumor microenvironment and help direct patients to suitable treatments.
This project tries to improve and test viral methods that control nerve cells with light in the visual system of the primate brain.
This project develops a gene therapy for Leber Congenital Amaurosis using a CRISPR base editor delivered to retinal pigment epithelium by silica nanocapsules.
This project holds a meeting on genetic medicines for cardiovascular disease, looking at emerging technologies and the challenges of turning discoveries into treatments.
This project studies how Mycobacterium tuberculosis moves lipids across its cell envelope, including transport systems that are entirely unknown.
This project expands a free open source package for biomolecular modeling and simulation and links it with machine learning frameworks.
This project uses deep learning to study how interactions between a host and its microorganisms change over time.
This project tries to find out how sensory nerves in the cornea protect it against bacterial binding through two receptors.
This project studies what one gene does in muscle cells and why its mutations lead to muscle symptoms in a disorder.
This project studies the role of one protein in hip osteoarthritis, a painful joint disease, using single-cell multi-omics approaches.
